change.title: pr-8
change.description: FIX: proper handling of group memberships
change.author: Régis Hanol

findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` gives 2 pages for 50 members at limit 50 (and 3 for 100). On page 1, `currentPage` is 1 and `totalPages` is 2, so `showingLast` is false and the "next" arrow stays enabled. `next` then sets offset to `min(0+50, 50) = 50`. `findMembers` requests offset 50 and the list goes empty on a phantom page "2/2". Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`. `currentPage` is consistent with that, since it uses the offset.

findings.title: Public group members page is now truncated to 50 members with no way to see the rest
findings.body: `GroupsController#members` now defaults to `limit` 50 for every group (`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22`). Before, only automatic groups were limited (200), and non-automatic groups returned all members. `group-members.js.es6:11` calls `model.findMembers()` once, and this template has no previous/next control and does not read `user_count`, `offset` or `limit`. Any non-automatic group with more than 50 members now silently shows only the first 50 alphabetically on `/groups/:name/members`. Either add pagination to this page or have it request enough rows.

findings.title: add_members raises a unique-index error when any listed user is already a member
findings.body: `group.add(user)` is `users.push(user)` (`app/models/group.rb:272`). That inserts a `group_users` row without checking existing membership. `group_users` has a unique index on (group_id, user_id) (`app/models/group_user.rb:18`). The old UI path went through `usernames=`, which diffed against current members, so re-listing an existing member was harmless. The new UI posts the raw input, and the input is never cleared (see the TODO in admin-group.js.es6). Adding "alice,bob" where alice is already in the group therefore raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and returns a 500. Users before the failing one may already have been added, because the pushes are not in a transaction. Skip users already in `group.users` (or use `group.users.exists?`), and add a spec for it.

findings.title: remove_member probably leaves groups.user_count stale
findings.body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` on a has_many :through deletes the join rows without running `GroupUser` destroy callbacks. The `user_count` counter cache lives on `GroupUser belongs_to :group, counter_cache: "user_count"` (`app/models/group_user.rb:2`). The through-association counter update looks for a `users_count` column, and the groups table has `user_count`. So the stored `user_count` is likely not decremented, and `BasicGroupSerializer`/the admin group list will show the old number after a reload. The UI hides this because `findMembers` overwrites `user_count` from a live `count`. The new spec only asserts `group.users.count`, not `user_count`. The existing `Group#remove` destroys the `GroupUser` rows, which fires the counter cache. Use `group.group_users.where(user_id: user_id).destroy_all`, or fix `Group#remove` and call it, and assert `group.user_count` in the spec. Also, `delete(id)` raises RecordNotFound (404) for a non-member id rather than being a no-op.

findings.title: `usernames` is never cleared or reset, so stale input can be added to another group
findings.body: `usernames` is a property on the singleton `adminGroup` controller. It is not reset in `setupController` (`admin_group_route.js:11`) and not cleared after `addMembers` (the TODO). After typing names for group A and switching to group B, clicking "Add" posts those names to B. After a successful add, a second click re-posts the same names, which hits the unique-index error in `add_members`. Clear `usernames` on success and when the model changes.

findings.title: Reload after removing the last member of the last page shows an empty page
findings.body: `removeMember` calls `findMembers()` with the current `offset`, clamped by the stale `user_count`. If the removed user was the only one on the last page, the server returns an empty `members` list for an offset past the new total. `currentPage` also still reports the old page until the response arrives. The admin sees an empty list with working "previous" navigation rather than being moved to the new last page. Consider clamping the offset to the last valid page after the count is updated.

findings.title: Response shape of GET /groups/:id/members changed but the spec still describes the old one
findings.body: The endpoint now returns `{members, meta: {total, limit, offset}}` instead of a bare array. `spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb:72-85` is still a `pending` pagination example that parses the body as an array. The "calls `posts_for`" example under `members` (lines 65-69) actually calls `:posts`. Nothing covers the new response or its `limit`/`offset`/`total` behaviour. Replace the pending example with one that covers the new JSON. Also, `limit` and `offset` are `to_i`'d without bounds, so a negative limit goes straight to SQL.

findings.title: Dead `#group-users` rule and a width rule that overrides the new one
findings.body: The group template now uses `id="user-selector"`, so `.row.groups input#group-users { width: 600px }` (line 1058) matches nothing. The `.row.groups input[type='text'] { width: 500px }` rule above it (line 1055) has higher specificity than the new `.groups .form-horizontal input { width: 350px }` rule. The 350px width applies only to non-text inputs inside the groups form, so the shared rule effectively sets 500px for the group name and user-selector. Remove the dead rule and decide on one width.

findings.title: remove_member spec uses PUT while the route is DELETE; edge cases are untested
findings.body: The route is `delete "members"`, but the automatic-group example does `xhr :put, :remove_member`. It passes only because Rails controller specs ignore the verb. Use `:delete`. There is also no example for adding a user who is already a member, a non-existent username, a non-member `user_id`, or `user_count` after add/remove. Those are the cases that the findings above show are broken or undefined.

contracts.action: Admin removes a member via the 'x' link in the group member list
contracts.equivalent_path: Group#remove (app/models/group.rb:276) destroys group_users rows, firing the counter cache; the old UI path removed members via PUT usernames=
contracts.before_after: Confirms with bootbox, then DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members.json with user_id, then reloads the member page. The server uses users.delete(id), which skips GroupUser callbacks.
contracts.visible_effect: The member disappears after findMembers returns. The list's user_count is overwritten by the live count in meta.total.
contracts.failure_mode: Ajax rejection goes to the global ajax error handling and the list is left unchanged. Stored groups.user_count is probably left stale server-side. The offset is not re-clamped if the last page empties.

contracts.action: Admin adds members by typing usernames in the user selector and clicking Add
contracts.equivalent_path: Old save path: PUT /admin/groups/:id with usernames, applied through Group#usernames= which diffed against current members
contracts.before_after: New path posts the raw comma list to PUT /admin/groups/:id/members. The server pushes each found user without checking existing membership, and unknown usernames are silently skipped. The input is not cleared afterwards.
contracts.visible_effect: List reloads with new members. Unknown usernames are ignored with no feedback.
contracts.failure_mode: An already-member username triggers a RecordNotUnique 500, partial adds are possible, and the error surfaces as a generic ajax error.

contracts.action: Member list paging (previous/next) and the initial load in setupController
contracts.equivalent_path: Old admin route afterModel blocked the transition on findMembers and then set `members`; the public group-members route did the same
contracts.before_after: Both routes now render immediately and call model.findMembers() unawaited in setupController. Results are written onto the shared Group model via setProperties. The Group objects come from the cached adminGroups list or from modelFor('group'), so limit/offset/members persist across revisits. The old behaviour gave each visit a fresh list.
contracts.visible_effect: The page renders with an empty list and a 0/0 pager, then fills in. Returning to a group keeps the previous offset and shows its old page until the reload finishes.
contracts.failure_mode: On rejection nothing is shown, with no retry or message beyond the global ajax handler. Overlapping responses (rapid next clicks) can land out of order and leave offset/members from an older request. The public members page has no pager, so groups with more than 50 members are truncated.

contracts.action: Create/save group via the split endpoints; add and remove membership routes
contracts.equivalent_path: Old PUT/PATCH /admin/groups/:id handled membership via usernames and a `changes` hash
contracts.before_after: POST and PUT /admin/groups/:id now accept flat params (name, visible, alias_level) and no usernames. PATCH changes handling is removed. The nested routes sit inside the AdminConstraint `resources :groups` block, so only admins reach them. Group.find on an unknown id gives 404.
contracts.visible_effect: New group is created without members, and the member section appears once `id` is set.
contracts.failure_mode: Any client still sending `group[...]`, `usernames` or PATCH changes is now ignored or gets 404. create ignores alias_level, as before.

summary: The refactor splits group membership out of save into add/remove endpoints and paginates the member list. I found two correctness bugs plus a public-page regression. totalPages is off by one for exact multiples of the page size, so the pager offers an empty extra page. The public /groups/:name/members page is now silently capped at 50 members with no pager. add_members will 500 when a listed user is already a member, because the input is never cleared and the server does not skip existing members. remove_member likely leaves the stored user_count stale. Smaller points: stale `usernames` carried across groups, a stale pending spec, a dead CSS rule, and a mislabelled HTTP verb in the new spec."}
